value.rationale: The compared protocols perform the same expected number of phase reset operations at each node but yield strictly different all-N noise allocation. This is a motivated mode-selective network design question: independent clocks uniformly reduce relative-phase disagreement while creating common-mode noise, whereas synchronized clocks remove common-mode wandering. Sharp exact closed formulas, including size and rate dependence, provide structural finite-network benchmarks rather than an arbitrary numerical case.
